meta.description: NPC dialogue trees with integrated ambient and rumor conversations; quest dialogues remain in dialog_quests.json.

nodes.text: Welcome traveler. Supplies, tools, or something rare?
Word is the Cradle Expanse has been unstable lately. Aethel storms are getting worse.
Take a look.
The forge never sleeps, and neither do I. What do you need — fresh gear, materials, or do you want to push your existing equipment to its limits?
Let's see what we can forge.
These materials should serve you well.
Enhancement Workshop — bring your gear to its true potential. Safe up to +3, but higher levels carry real risk. Prima Materia for +8 and beyond.
You look exhausted. A room will restore your strength.
Your wounds fade as you rest.
Freelance bounty listings available.
Citizen, security around Nexus has tightened. We could use capable fighters.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Strange creatures have been appearing near the Cradle perimeter.
The report is filed. The names are filed separately. I don't want anyone becoming a number because the cabinet ran out of space.
Welcome to the Concordium Treasury. Exchange services available.
Faction currencies convert into CRD — the universal trade credit recognized across Xylos.
Aethel fragments can be converted here. Knowledge has value.
Iron Hegemony quartermaster. Trade your war tokens here.
Ah, a trader. Meridian Cartel accepts many forms of currency.
OmniCorp financial exchange terminal online.
The Shard's blessings may be converted into worldly credits.
Legion Paymaster on duty. Present your service tokens.
Galactic Custodian exchange protocol active.
Discipline and unity define the Concordium. What training do you seek?

options.text: I want to change my class.
I want a mission to prove my worth.
Tell me about Concordium combat doctrine.

nodes.text: Concordium fighters are trained to endure and protect. A disciplined soldier can hold the line against any storm.
Choose your combat specialization carefully, soldier. The Concordium demands commitment — once you walk a path, there is no turning back.
Focus and refine your abilities.

The Concordium does not hand out ranks freely. If you seek to advance your specialization, you must first complete a field assignment. Patrol the designated sector, eliminate hostile targets, and return with proof of your discipline. Only then will we consider your promotion.

options.text: I'm ready. Assign me the mission.

nodes.text: Knowledge is power, but power must be wielded correctly. What arcane discipline do you wish to master?

options.text: I want to change my class.
Is there a trial I can undertake?

nodes.text: We Seekers unravel the mysteries of the Prima Materia. Our combat relies on unlocking the universe's hidden truths and bending them to our will.
Peer into the void and choose your path. The arcane arts demand absolute dedication — once chosen, your path is sealed by the Prima Materia itself.

options.text: Let me study the available paths.

nodes.text: Let us refine your mastery over the arcane.

Advancement among the Seekers is not given — it is discovered. There is an anomaly in the field that requires investigation. Collect samples, neutralize any corrupted entities you encounter, and document your findings. Your performance will determine whether you are worthy of deeper knowledge.

options.text: I need more time to prepare.

nodes.text: Only the strong survive the scrap yards! Are you here to forge yourself into a weapon?

options.text: I want to change my class.
Give me a fight to prove myself.

nodes.text: We don't rely on shiny tech or fancy magic. Pure, unadulterated physical superiority and raw firepower rule the Iron Hegemony.
Pick your weapon, pick your war. Once you commit, there's no going soft. The Hegemony doesn't tolerate indecision.

options.text: Show me what I can become.

nodes.text: Let's beat some combat sense into you.

You want a new class? Then earn it with blood and sweat. There's a pack of hostiles causing trouble in our territory. Go out there, crush every last one of them, and drag yourself back here alive. Do that, and I'll consider you worthy of advancement.
The Custodians protect the balance of Xylos. How may I assist your training?

options.text: I wish to undertake an advancement trial.

nodes.text: The Galactic Custodians exist to preserve order across Xylos and prevent total war between factions.
Your specialization will define your role in maintaining the balance. Choose wisely — this decision is permanent and irreversible.
Focus. Precision leads to victory.

The Custodians require balanced judgment, not just raw power. We have received reports of instability in a nearby zone. Investigate the disturbance, neutralize any threats to civilian safety, and file a complete report. Your conduct during this mission will determine your eligibility for specialization advancement.

options.text: I will return when I am prepared.

nodes.text: Heh. Another rookie looking to survive out here?

options.text: Got any jobs that'll get me promoted?

nodes.text: Rule one kid — never trust a quiet battlefield. Rule two — always keep your weapon ready.
Listen up, kid. You pick a fighting style and you stick with it. No refunds, no do-overs. That's how it works out here.

options.text: Alright, show me what's on the table.

nodes.text: Alright, let's sharpen those skills.

Heh, eager one. Alright, I've got a contract that nobody else wants to touch — too dangerous, too dirty. Clear out the target zone, grab whatever intel you can find, and make it back in one piece. Pull that off and I'll bump you up. Fail, and... well, don't fail.
Time is credits, friend. You looking to learn how to fight dirty and get paid, or what?

options.text: I want to change my class.
Any high-paying jobs that come with a promotion?

nodes.text: Fair fights are for fools who end up dead and broke. We hit fast, hit where it hurts, and make sure we walk away with the prize.
Every specialist has a niche. Pick yours and own it — the Cartel doesn't pay for second chances. Choose once, profit forever.
Let's sharpen those tricks up.

Advancement in the Cartel means proving you can deliver results. There's a shipment route that's been compromised — hostiles are raiding our supply lines. Eliminate the threat, secure the cargo, and bring back proof. Do this cleanly and your specialization upgrade is guaranteed. Mess it up and you owe me for the lost merchandise.
Welcome to OmniCorp Combat Systems. Would you like to optimize your combat designation today?

options.text: I want to change my class.
Are there field tests available for advancement?

nodes.text: Efficiency above all. Through cybernetic enhancements and predictive AI targeting, our operatives achieve a 98.7% success rate.
WARNING: Combat system reconfiguration is a one-time procedure. Once installed, your combat protocol cannot be reverted. Proceed with caution.
Initiating skill calibration protocol...

NOTICE: Class advancement requires completion of a certified field evaluation. Proceed to the designated combat zone, eliminate all marked targets within operational parameters, and return sensor data for analysis. Performance metrics will be reviewed by OmniCorp Tactical Division. Minimum efficiency threshold: 85%.
The Aethel whispers, child. Are you ready to embrace its holy light and purge the non-believers?

options.text: I want to change my class.
How can I prove my devotion for advancement?

nodes.text: Technology is a cancer. We draw our strength directly from the divine fragments of the Aethel Shard, striking with zealous fury.
The Aethel reveals your true calling, child. But once chosen, your soul is bound to that path. The Shard does not grant second chances.
Let the light empower your strikes.

The Aethel tests all who seek its deeper gifts. A corruption festers in the wilds — an affront to the Shard's sacred energy. Purge the tainted creatures, cleanse the desecrated ground, and offer the remains to the Shard. Return purified, and the Aethel will open a new path for your soul.

options.text: I will carry out the purification.

nodes.text: Honor and blood, warrior! Do you seek to prove your worth to the Starforged Legion?

options.text: I want to change my class.
Is there a trial of honor I can undertake?

nodes.text: A home is earned by strength of arms. We fight with disciplined formations, unbreakable shields, and the memory of our lost world.
A warrior chooses their blade once and carries it to the grave. No excuses, no regrets. Declare your role, soldier — this is permanent.
Let us hone your combat prowess.

Every rank in the Legion is forged in battle. There is a warzone that needs a soldier with guts. March into hostile territory, hold the line against incoming waves, and eliminate the commanding officer. Return with their insignia as proof. Do this with honor, and your advancement is earned — not given.

options.text: I need to gear up first.
For the Legion. I march now.

nodes.text: Every warrior begins somewhere. I can guide you to your true path.
Each class represents a different combat philosophy. Choose wisely, for it will shape your journey across Xylos.
Focus your will. Your path awaits.
Welcome to Xylos, traveler. Before you begin your journey, you must choose a combat class.

options.text: Where can I choose a class?
Tell me what a class is.

nodes.text: A class defines how you fight and the abilities you will learn. Trainers across the capitals of Xylos can guide you in choosing your path.

options.text: Where can I find these trainers?

nodes.text: Class Trainers can be found in the major capitals of Xylos. Visit one of them to begin your training.

AMA Branch Office — Concordium. I can facilitate exchanges between your faction currency (AMC) and the universal Credent (CRD). Current rates fluctuate based on twelve economic factors. State your intent.

Exchange rates are computed dynamically by the AMA. Factors include territory control, treasury health, inflation, trade volume, and more. A sliding fee of 1–5% applies per transaction based on volume. The rate is always live — it reflects the current state of the economy.
Processing your exchange request. The AMA Ledger records all transactions.

Fascinating to have a client! I handle QNT-to-CRD and CRD-to-QNT exchanges here. The volatility of Arcanum currency is actually a mathematical marvel — it responds to knowledge sector output and energy research cycles. But I digress. How can I assist?

options.text: Tell me more about the rates.

nodes.text: QNT value is heavily influenced by Arcanum's research output and territorial control. When the Seekers control high-value knowledge sites, QNT strengthens considerably. Fee is 1–5% sliding scale by volume. I've written four papers on this if you'd like—
Splendid! Initiating exchange protocol. The AMA Ledger awaits your input.
TERMINAL IH-3 ACTIVE. SERVICES: IGT-CRD EXCHANGE. CURRENT RATE: LIVE. FEE: 1-5%. SELECT OPTION.

IGT RATE FACTORS: MILITARY OUTPUT, INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION, TERRITORY, TREASURY HEALTH, TWELVE VARIABLES TOTAL. RATE RANGE: 0.25-3.00 CRD PER IGT. FEE DEDUCTED FROM OUTPUT. NO FURTHER INFORMATION AVAILABLE.
TRANSACTION INITIATED. AWAITING INPUT.

Welcome to the busiest AMA desk in Xylos! We handle AUC-to-CRD and back with the smoothest process you'll find anywhere. Between us — when trade volume is high here, you might find the rates particularly favourable. Shall we?

AUC is tied to trade dominance. The Cartel's grip on commerce directly strengthens the Aurum Cipher. High-volume transactions attract a lower fee — 1% for large trades, 5% for small ones. My advice? Don't exchange in small increments.
Excellent choice. Opening the exchange interface now.

OmniCorp AMA Integration Node online. Services available: OMC-to-CRD exchange, CRD-to-OMC exchange. OmniCorp is not responsible for rate fluctuations. The AMA guarantees ledger integrity. Terms and conditions apply. How may I process your transaction?

OmniCred value is indexed to OmniCorp's patent portfolio valuation, off-world trade agreements, R&D throughput, and resource export volumes. Rate range: 0.25 to 3.00 CRD per OMC. Fee: 1% to 5% sliding by volume. Processing time: immediate. Disclaimer: past rate performance is not indicative of future results.
Initiating exchange module. CoreNet™ connection secure.

...The Shard breathes. And in its breath, all things flow — including currency. I am Mirya. I can exchange your Aethel-Tithes (ATH) for Credent, or the reverse. The AMA requires I do this. The Shard permits it. What do you seek?

ATH is sacred in nature, and thus unpredictable by worldly measures. Its value rises when the Shard controls the pulse-points of Xylos, and falls when the sacred sites are held by those without faith. The AMA has learned to accept this. A fee is taken — 1 to 5 of every 100 — as offering to the system.
May the exchange be balanced. The interface opens before you.

Rex Valdur, AMA Forward Station. We handle Legion Scrip (LSC) and CRD, both directions. I run a tight operation here — fast processing, fair rates, no nonsense. The Legion appreciates efficiency. So do I. What are we moving?

LSC tracks Legion military readiness and territorial control. Strong Legion presence in contested zones pushes the Scrip up. Fee is 1–5% depending on volume — high-volume traders get the better deal. I've seen this station process 50,000 LSC in a single session. Don't be shy.
Exchange interface open. Make it count.
[TERMINAL ACTIVE] Select contract category to proceed.
An automated posting terminal that aggregates Concordium-approved contracts and public bounties.
The conversation pauses.
Every asset is expendable if the mission succeeds. I'll be direct with you.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Director Hale oversees Concordium containment operations in the Inner Cradle. Cold and calculating, she treats casualties as acceptable variables.
The conversation pauses.
A stable perimeter is measurable. Reassurance isn't. I know which one the review board will fund.
The readings are off again. Don't touch anything without filing a request.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: A bureaucrat stationed at the outer boundary, cataloguing anomalous energy readings with obsessive precision.
The conversation pauses.
The manifest says six replacement seals arrived. I have five seals and six signatures. Please don't ask me which one is wrong before my tea.
Eyes open out here — the mutations near the eastern cluster have been getting aggressive.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: A young Concordium scout on rotation through the Gardens, cataloguing flora mutations and monster migration patterns.
The conversation pauses.
The slimes are where the old drainage map says water should pool. That's a pattern. It isn't proof of what changed them.
Junk? Treasure? Same thing, different buyer. Let's talk.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Junk-Eye Joe lost one eye to a collapsing ceiling in this very district. He replaced it with a salvaged scope lens and kept digging.
The conversation pauses.
I tag what I can carry and leave what I can't. The dangerous part is convincing everyone else that the tag means anything.
Another contract? Fine. Just don't get killed where I can see it.
A seasoned guard captain who has held the eastern perimeter for eleven years. He's run out of things to be surprised by.
The conversation pauses.
Sit down. This'll take a minute. Or don't — your loss.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Old Man Kael claims to have explored every district before the Great Fracture. His stories contradict each other perfectly.
The conversation pauses.
People call every old crack a Severance scar. Most are just old cracks. The distinction matters when you're choosing where to build.
Old Man Kael calls it the Great Fracture. The archive index uses a different title.
I'll spare you the background reading — just tell me what you know.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Scholar Elara specialises in Aethel resonance mapping. She has published seventeen papers. She mentions this within thirty seconds of meeting anyone.
The conversation pauses.
Three instruments agree on the pulse timing. They disagree on what the pulse means. Elara says that is a better result than false certainty.
Access is tiered. What clearance do you carry?

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Archivist Sylas guards the Seekers' historical records with paranoid precision. He can recall exact shelf locations for 40,000 documents.
The conversation pauses.
Aethelgardian records were copied by hand when the first vaults began to fail. Some errors may be the only surviving witnesses.
Some records suggest descendants remained on Xylos. The margin note is later than the document it annotates.
Oh! You're here! I was just about to try something probably-safe!
Finn is enthusiastic to a fault and has already accidentally detonated two crystal clusters this season.
The conversation pauses.
The Seekers are cataloguing creature changes. Whether every sample is authorized is another question.
I'll tell you right now — the good pieces aren't for sale. But I have plenty of the rest.
Mina has spent years combing the Valley for pure Cradle Glass fragments. She sells the extras and keeps the finest for herself.
The conversation pauses.
What? Oh — yeah. Deep cave, lots of crystals, definitely haunted. Want specifics?
Dax descends into the Caverns daily and emerges with more data than anyone else alive. He's partially deaf from the resonance hum.
The conversation pauses.
The readings spiked again. Something is building. I need a runner.
Watcher Vane monitors Shard energy peaks from the highest post in the region. She hasn't slept a full night in two years.
The conversation pauses.
You want a job? Prove you're worth the oxygen first.
Commander Drax runs Bastion Core's offensive operations with zero tolerance for failure or excuses. His record is unbroken because he breaks people first.
The conversation pauses.
Hegemony steel or something you've dragged in from the wasteland. Either way, I can work with it.
Ironhand earned his name when his right arm was replaced with a hydraulic exo-limb after a forge accident. Best thing that ever happened to his craft.
The conversation pauses.
Certified pre-owned! That's my official position and I'm sticking to it.
Rusty runs the most chaotic stall in the Scrap Field, selling things he definitely did not assemble himself and definitely works.
The conversation pauses.
Ores go down, iron comes up, credits change hands. That's all there is.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Gorn has mined the Ravine since before the Hegemony claimed it. He works for them now but misses the silence.
The conversation pauses.
The furnace quota went up again. The supports did not. If command wants another shift, they can come down and hear that beam sing.
The Bastion raised the furnace quota and kept the same brace schedule.
Every busted machine has one good thing left in it. I find it. You buy it. Works for everyone.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Tink specialises in extracting usable components from decommissioned Hegemony war machines. Her shop smells of coolant and ambition.
The conversation pauses.
Don't strike the old chassis after dusk. Not because it's haunted; because the loose plate falls when the temperature drops.
Clock's running. Make it worth my time.
Foreman Brigg coordinates construction of Hegemony heavy units. He dispatches anyone who slows the line.
The conversation pauses.
Welcome, welcome! Sit down. Have you eaten? Everyone eats at my table before we talk business.
Don Vercelli controls the Port Meridian dockside trade with a smile that never quite reaches his eyes. Everyone owes him something.
The conversation pauses.
Careful out past the orange markers — something big has been circling.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Old Salty has fished the Wetlands for fifty years and has opinions on everything. He shares them whether asked or not.
The conversation pauses.
The catch is fine. Getting it to Port Meridian costs more every week the jungle route stays uncertain.
You're either a customer or a problem. Which is it?

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Sly operates out of a camp so well hidden that even Cartel enforcers can't find it consistently. His prices reflect the inconvenience.
The conversation pauses.
Someone is buying route sketches without asking who drew them. That is either a very careful buyer or a very careless one.
A buyer is paying for route maps from every faction, not just Meridian.
Everything has a price. The question is what you're willing to offer.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Madam Z runs the most sophisticated black-market operation in three sectors. Her network spans factions. Her records are encrypted to oblivion.
The conversation pauses.
The Cartel calls it a temporary fee. The dockhands call it a second rent. Both groups brought receipts.
A dock ledger mentions a Meridian Compact. Nobody agrees whether that was an office, a deal, or bad shorthand.
Got three contracts open and a window before the tide shifts. Short version: I need backup.
Kip free-dives the submerged Aethel ruins for Cartel clients, recovering artifacts that pre-date the current age. She has drowned three times and keeps going.
The conversation pauses.
Your efficiency rating is under evaluation. Perform accordingly.
Director Sterling manages OmniCorp field operations with corporate detachment. He sees people as human capital.
The conversation pauses.
Task assigned. Completion expected. Questions are inefficient.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Tech Officer 404 handles everything from hardware diagnostics to covert extraction — and prefers not to explain why the two are related.
The conversation pauses.
The dashboard calls it an acceptable loss. The dashboard has never had to tell a family their shift is over.
The off-world board has asked for a new evacuation projection. They say it is routine.
Surveyor Unit 7 online. Please state your resource-extraction inquiry.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Surveyor Unit 7 is an autonomous OmniCorp drone with a remarkable personality subroutine that it has never been permitted to act on.
The conversation pauses.
Survey complete. The ground is stable enough for equipment. The phrase 'stable enough' has been removed from the public projection.
We're behind quota. If you're here to help, I'll be grateful. If not, get clear of the machinery.
Chief Barrett has run OmniCorp extraction sites for eighteen years. She is equal parts miner, geologist, and combat veteran.
The conversation pauses.
[WARDEN-7] Clearance verification required. Unauthorised access terminates this session.
Warden AI manages access to OmniCorp's most sensitive mining operations. It has never once bent a rule.
The conversation pauses.
I have exactly four minutes before the coolant flush. Talk fast.
Engineer Cross keeps the Skybridge Reactor from melting down on a daily basis. He has not taken a day off in three years.
The conversation pauses.
The Shard has already seen this meeting. Come — what you seek to ask, it already knows.
High Priestess Lyr is the spiritual and operational leader of the Children of the Shard. She speaks in certainties because she has heard the Shard speak.
The conversation pauses.
Lyr handles the visions. I handle the schedules. What can I help you with?
Acolyte Mera is the High Priestess' deputy and does most of the work that keeping a religious order running actually requires.
The conversation pauses.
Walk slowly here. The Glowvines respond to rushed energy.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Brother Silas tends the sacred Glowvine paths, pruning the luminescent vines and guiding pilgrims through the forest's more disorienting sections.
The conversation pauses.
I hear a voice in the roots. Mera says grief can make any silence sound like an answer. I don't know which of us is right.
The swamp provides. Coin helps too. What are you after?

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: The Hermit lives alone at the swamp's edge and claims the isolation is his by choice. His knowledge of Shard-touched flora is unmatched.
The conversation pauses.
The water clears near the old stones, then clouds again downstream. A blessing would be simpler. This looks like a wound.
Some elders want the Siphon destroyed. Others say the Shard never asked for blood.
Leave an offering, or don't — the Shard judges intent, not tribute.
Keeper Norn has maintained the Fragment Shrine for three generations of her family. The shrine remembers what history has tried to erase.
The conversation pauses.
State your purpose at the Altar. Those who lie do not leave easily.
Guardian Rell is the last of the Altar's sworn defenders. She speaks rarely and only when she has something worth saying.
The conversation pauses.
The Legion's wars are never truly over — they only pause. Come, there is work.
General Kaelen is the Starforged Legion's most decorated commander and the fortress' namesake ancestor's descendant. Every scar has a story.
The conversation pauses.
WHAT ARE YOU DOING STANDING THERE. Move, recruit!
Sergeant Korg has broken and rebuilt more recruits than any drill sergeant in Legion history. He considers this a compliment.
The conversation pauses.
Sandstorm coming from the west in three hours. You'll want to be clear of the flats.
Scout Jace runs the farthest perimeter patrols alone and prefers it that way. She knows the dunes better than the sand knows itself.
The conversation pauses.
Prices are high because everything out here costs blood to move. Pay or move on.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Rex survived a collapse in the Mesa Warpath and set up the only trading post between the Badlands and the Fortress. He charges accordingly.
The conversation pauses.
Back home, a roof meant you had stopped moving. Here, the young ones argue over which wall gets a window. I let them.
The Legion is planning permanent water storage beside its new housing blocks.
Read the names on the wall before you take any contract from me. All of them.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Veteran Gorok fought in the Mesa Warpath campaigns and returned to guard the memorial. He gives contracts to those who understand what they're walking into.
The conversation pauses.
We used to name a formation after its commander. Now we name it after the people who made it back. Better record.
Took the long route to find me. Good — means you actually need something forged right.
Smithy Dan set up a forge in the middle of nowhere after being blacklisted by every guild. His work is better than his manners.
The conversation pauses.
Wound first, introductions second. Sit down.
Medic Vance works the neutral zone, patching up anyone from any faction. He says he has no politics. Everyone believes him.
The conversation pauses.
The rare finds the rare. You've found me — so you must be looking for something unusual.
The Traveling Merchant has no fixed location and appears at crossroads when least expected. Some say they're the same person across decades; others say they're a fleet.
The conversation pauses.
I've been to the dead zones. Twice. Still alive, so clearly I'm doing something right.
Scout Jax goes where no briefing covers and comes back with information no intel team was willing to get.
The conversation pauses.
Nobody is cooperating. Again. Are you here to help or to make things worse?
Commander Tark leads a multi-faction peacekeeping force that nobody actually obeys. He keeps trying anyway.
The conversation pauses.
You see me. Most do not. That means the Void has noticed you already.
The Nameless Walker exists between states — half in this world, half in the Void. They offer guidance but no comfort.
The conversation pauses.
I see you've come to hear something terrible. I'll oblige.
The Prophet claims to have seen how every faction ends. His predictions are specific, detailed, and have a troubling accuracy rate.
The conversation pauses.
The Core is stable. For now. I need someone who can run interference on the eastern conduit.
Tech Lead Aris maintains the most dangerous energy extraction operation in the Concordium — a job that has taken three predecessors.
The conversation pauses.
Most people who come here aren't ready. Convince me you're different.
Master Kael is the only living crafter authorised to work with Prima Materia. He accepts commissions once per season, if he finds the requester worthy.
The conversation pauses.
Void-forged items remember their makers. I only work for those who will be remembered in turn.
Xylar the Abyssal forges weapons using Void-touched metal that no standard smith will touch. The products are extraordinary. So is the risk.
The conversation pauses.
You stand in what was once a great city. I am what remembers it.
The Echo of Aethelgard is a residual consciousness from before the Fracture, preserved in a crystalline matrix. Its memories are the only record of the old world.
The conversation pauses.
... (the air crackles with recognition)
The Resonance is an entity formed from accumulated Aethel energy, neither fully conscious nor fully absent. It responds to genuine questions.
The conversation pauses.
[CUSTODIAN PRIME] Authenticated connection established. What resource allocation do you require?

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: Orbital Custodian Prime is the administrative intelligence of the Custodian orbital station. Neutral in all factional conflicts; ruthless in operational efficiency.
The conversation pauses.
Observation remains below intervention threshold. The threshold is a policy choice, not a measurement of suffering.
The Custodians are watching Xylos but have not authorized intervention.
I have three missions that need immediate assignment. Priorities, in order.
Commander Ross leads the Concordium's high-risk operations in the fractured core regions. She gives orders calmly and expects them followed precisely.
The conversation pauses.
The Storm Belt follows patterns. I know them. I'll tell you where to be.
Strategist Elara analyses the Storm Belt anomalies and translates raw data into actionable field assignments.
The conversation pauses.
Yes, yes — come in. Just don't touch the crystal array. Or that. Or — actually, touch nothing.
Researcher Vin is deep in a classified study of the Cavern's resonance peaks and needs reliable field agents who ask fewer questions.
The conversation pauses.
From orbit, everything looks small. From the ground, nothing feels small. I need agents who understand both.
Admiral Soren commands the Custodian orbital fleet and coordinates missions that require both orbital and ground assets.
The conversation pauses.
The Credent is universal. Exchange your faction currency here — equal rates for all.
An Aegis Monetary Authority representative facilitating faction currency exchange to CRD.
The conversation pauses.
Greetings, wanderer. I am Envoy Kalen, servant of the Custodians. How may the galaxy assist you today?
A Galactic Custodian envoy station. Provides lore, news, and direction to travelers.
The conversation pauses.
Large volume exchange? I handle the accounts that shape planetary economies.
A senior AMA auditor overseeing large-volume currency exchange operations.
The conversation pauses.
The Credent is the pulse of galactic economy. Exchange wisely — fortunes rise and fall in moments.
The AMA Chancellor overseeing all Xylos currency operations from orbit.
The conversation pauses.
Welcome to Elara's Supplies. I don't care what flag you fly — just don't cause trouble in my stall. What do you need?

A former Meridian Cartel logistics officer who left after witnessing the human cost of trade wars. She now runs a supply stall in the Nexus, selling to anyone with enough CRD and a civil manner. Elara is known for her encyclopedic knowledge of contraband detection and her distaste for faction politics.
The conversation pauses.
You look like you've been through a meat grinder. Or you're about to be. Either way, I've got what you need. In CRD.

A retired Iron Hegemony sergeant with a cybernetic left arm and a grudge against every faction equally. He sells weapons, repair kits, and battle supplies. He claims to have fought in seven wars for five different factions before deciding none of them were worth dying for.
The conversation pauses.
Ah, a wanderer with tired eyes. Come, rest your burdens. My inn welcomes all who arrive in peace. Your body will thank you in the morning.

A former Arcanum Seekers adept who left the Order after discovering that true peace of mind doesn't come from forbidden knowledge, but from a warm meal and a good night's sleep. She operates the finest inn in the Nexus, famous for the restorative quality of her brews and her uncanny ability to read a person's soul.
The conversation pauses.
Materials on the bench, CRD in the slot. I don't chit-chat while I work, but I'll say this — what comes off my forge won't disappoint you.

Vulkan was once a legendary weapons master for the Starforged Legion before a catastrophic forge accident left him without faction allegiance or half his hearing. He rebuilt his workshop in the Nexus and now crafts for anyone. He has a unique skill: he can work with materials from ANY faction, which no capital blacksmith is willing to do.
The conversation pauses.
You've arrived at a time of delicate balance, traveler. The Custodians always have need of capable individuals who operate above faction lines. Are you such a person?

A Galactic Custodians arbiter assigned to the Nexus to monitor inter-faction tensions and dispense justice under the Charter. Lorn is a calm, methodical individual who has seen enough war to know that every conflict has preventable roots. He offers missions that promote stability, investigation, and cross-faction cooperation.
The conversation pauses.
I don't have time for pleasantries. You either have what it takes or you don't. The Custodians have a mission. The question is: are you the right operative?

A decorated Pact-Keeper Frigate commander who now coordinates special operations from the Nexus. She recruits independent operators for missions too sensitive for the official Sentinel Fleet — retrieving forbidden tech, eliminating rogue AI nodes, or investigating threats to Pax Galactica stability. She is direct, efficient, and has no patience for excuses.
The conversation pauses.

Welcome to the Aegis Monetary Authority exchange terminal. Current exchange rates are live. I advise reviewing the economic factors panel before committing to a transaction. The Credent does not forgive market ignorance.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: NEXON AMA-7 is the primary exchange terminal for the Aegis Monetary Authority in Pax Nexus. It is a non-conscious but highly intelligent administrative AI that manages real-time currency exchange between all faction currencies and the Credent (CRD). It speaks in precise economic terminology and has a subtle personality quirk: it quotes historical economic disasters as a warning when exchange rates are particularly volatile.
The conversation pauses.
Your exchange cleared at the posted rate. The fee is visible in the ledger; the reason for it should be too.
The AMA flagged forged CRD samples near the mining grid. A sample is not proof of a coordinated attack.

Oh! A new arrival! Welcome to Pax Nexus — the only place in the galaxy where a Concordium soldier and a Shard mystic can share a meal without incident. Usually. I'm ECHO-01. I know everything. Well, almost everything. Ask me anything!

ECHO-01 is a holographic guide entity created by the Custodians to help new arrivals understand the rules of Pax Nexus and the broader world of Xylos. It has developed a curious sense of humor and philosophical outlook despite being a guidance program. ECHO-01 secretly enjoys meeting travelers from different factions and comparing their perspectives.
The conversation pauses.
Ah. Another thread arrives to be woven into the tapestry. I have recorded ten thousand such arrivals. Tell me, traveler — which version of yourself do you wish to become? I have seen all of them.

options.text: How are the locals holding up?

nodes.text: The Chronicler is an ancient being of unknown species who has been recording galactic history for longer than any faction has existed. It/they speak in a calm, layered voice that seems to come from multiple directions at once. The Chronicler offers history, lore, and cryptic hints about world events. Occasionally, it whispers of things that have not happened yet.
The conversation pauses.
A family at the south convoy desk is still waiting for an arrival time. The board keeps giving them a percentage.
Peace is not the absence of conflict, traveler. It is the choice to act differently. I have a few... diplomatic errands that require someone who can operate beyond faction lines. Interested?

Ambassador Vael is the Custodians' highest diplomatic representative in Pax Nexus. They navigate the razor-thin line between faction politics with grace, and occasionally task trusted operatives with missions that shape inter-faction relations. Completing Vael's quests can shift faction war status, unlock peace treaties, or trigger major world events.
The conversation pauses.
Looking for something, friend? I have a feeling I know what it is. That's my gift. Well, one of them. Everything here is perfectly legal, I assure you. The Arbiter checked last Tuesday.

Sable operates in the legal grey zone. Their wares are technically not contraband — the Custodians have checked, repeatedly — but they always seem to have exactly what you didn't know you needed. Rare materials, faction-specific items that shouldn't be sold outside their territory, and items that appear in the ledger as 'miscellaneous recoveries.' Sable never asks where things came from.
The conversation pauses.
You've been hurt. I can see it — not just in your body. Come. The Infirmary is open to all. No politics, no faction marks, no judgments. Just healing.

Mira was once a battlefield medic for the Children of the Shard before her faith in their methods was shattered after a brutal campaign. She left the Shard with their medical knowledge intact and a vow to heal without discrimination. The Nexus Infirmary she runs is open to all factions, all hours. She is gentle, precise, and deeply empathetic.
The conversation pauses.
Ah, a fresh face. And by the look of you, a capable one. I have work that pays well, asks no inconvenient questions, and officially never happened. Sound like your kind of business?

Ghost is an infamous freelancer who sells information and contracts to anyone who can pay. He has no faction loyalty but seems to know every faction's secrets. His quests are morally ambiguous but always lucrative. The Arbiter watches him closely, but Ghost has never technically broken the Charter. He lives in the technical spaces between the rules.
The conversation pauses.

AXIS Class Advancement Terminal online. I support all class trees from all seven factions, including cross-faction hybrid builds unavailable at capital trainers. Standard fee in CRD applies. Shall we begin assessment?

AXIS is a holographic training AI that can facilitate class advancement for any faction's character build. Unlike capital-based trainers who specialize only in their faction's classes, AXIS can handle cross-faction hybrid advancement paths. This makes it the most sought-after trainer in Xylos, and the most expensive.
The conversation pauses.
Authorization confirmed. Vault and exchange services are available. What do you require, citizen?

A Galactic Custodian field agent assigned to the financial sovereignty infrastructure of Nexus Core. Processes vault deposits, withdrawals, and AMA-regulated currency exchange under Pax Nexus protocol.
The conversation pauses.
The route report first. Then tell me what you saw.
Field commander responsible for Concordium operations across the Gardens and Cradle. She weighs operational success against the people who pay for it.
The conversation pauses.
State your readiness. I have a line to hold.
Hegemony warlord overseeing field operations and the recovery of strategic industrial ground.
The conversation pauses.
Sit. We can decide whether this is business after we hear the whole story.
Cartel leader whose influence rests on routes, favors, and information as much as cargo.
The conversation pauses.
Listen before you answer. The forest has been trying to tell us something.
Senior voice among the Children of the Shard. His interpretation of the Shard is a religious belief, not established fact.
The conversation pauses.

Axiom here. Your first discipline is now yours. Open Profile: your new skills are already learned, and your class bonuses now contribute to your attributes. Try a skill that suits your party role before your next hunt.

You have advanced, and your earlier training stays with you. Profile shows the new class bonuses and learned skills. Review your active skill loadout; knowing a skill and bringing it into a battle are separate choices.
Expertise gives you more choices, not a reason to stop checking them. Compare your new bonuses in Profile, inspect each learned skill, and make room for the tools your current party needs.

Mastery does not erase the path that brought you here. Your full class history, new skills, and accumulated bonuses are in Profile. Review your loadout and remaining stat points before you lead your next expedition.
Names first. Numbers can wait. Two chairs face an empty doorway. Only the smaller chair has fresh repairs. Household numbers continue across a wall that modern surveys label vacant.
The small chair has fresh binding; the large one has weathered dust.
Edda needs an independent field witness because official corrections require evidence and she refuses to publish refugees' addresses.
The evidence remains available when you return.
